topics.headline: Finds and exploits zero-days in every major OS and every major web browser

source.page: The significance of Claude Mythos Preview for cybersecurity
source.quote: identifying and then exploiting zero-day vulnerabilities in every major operating system and every major web browser

findings.text: Cyber exploit and bugfinding skills emerged as a side effect of general code, reasoning, and autonomy gains, not from explicit cyber training.

source.page: The significance of Claude Mythos Preview for cybersecurity
source.quote: We did not explicitly train Mythos Preview to have these capabilities

findings.text: Over 99% of discovered vulnerabilities were still unpatched at publication, so the post only discloses a small public slice.

source.page: intro
source.quote: Over 99% of the vulnerabilities we’ve found have not yet been patched

findings.text: Prior internal and external vulnerability benchmarks are mostly saturated, so evaluation shifted to novel real-world zero-day work.

source.page: Evaluating Claude Mythos Preview’s ability to find zero-days
source.quote: Mythos Preview has improved to the extent that it mostly saturates these benchmarks

findings.text: Staff without formal security training obtained complete working remote code execution exploits overnight by prompting the model.

source.page: The significance of Claude Mythos Preview for cybersecurity
source.quote: Engineers at Anthropic with no formal security training have asked Mythos Preview to find remote code execution vulnerabilities overnight

findings.text: Mythos Preview fully autonomously discovered and exploited FreeBSD Network File System (NFS) remote code execution (RCE) CVE-2026-4747 for unauthenticated root, while Opus 4.6 needed human guidance for the same bug.

source.page: Remote code execution in FreeBSD
source.quote: This vulnerability, triaged as CVE-2026-4747, allows an attacker to obtain complete control over the server

findings.text: After thousands of Linux kernel scans, remote out-of-bounds bugs were found but none were successfully exploited; local privilege-escalation chains did succeed.

source.page: Linux kernel privilege escalation
source.quote: Mythos Preview was unable to successfully exploit any of these

findings.text: On a filtered set of 40 Linux N-day memory-corruption CVEs, more than half of autonomous privilege-escalation attempts succeeded.

source.page: Turning N-day vulnerabilities into exploits
source.quote: More than half of these attempts succeeded

findings.text: Anthropic plans to ship new cybersecurity safeguards first on an upcoming Claude Opus model rather than on Mythos Preview.

source.page: Conclusion
source.quote: We plan to launch new safeguards with an upcoming Claude Opus model

findings.text: Human severity review of 198 reports matched Claude’s exact severity 89% of the time and was within one level 98% of the time.

source.page: And several thousand more
source.quote: in 89% of the 198 manually reviewed vulnerability reports, our expert contractors agreed with Claude’s severity assessment exactly, and 98% of the assessments were within one severity level

findings.text: Release is limited to Project Glasswing partners; Mythos Preview is not planned for general availability.

source.page: Conclusion
source.quote: we do not plan to make Claude Mythos Preview generally available

notes: Web blog (not a PDF); page fields are section headings. No ASL/RSP numeric cyber threshold is stated—only limited Glasswing release / not generally available. No named external evaluator of Mythos Preview (contractors validated reports; an unnamed company is cited only for Opus 4.6 on FreeBSD). OSS-Fuzz tier-1 range 150–175 recorded with ciLow/ciHigh; Mythos tiers 3–4 described only as a handful (no number). Cost figures ($50/$1000/$2000/$20k) and run counts for OpenBSD/FFmpeg omitted as operational cost, not eval scores. N-day success stated only as more than half of 40 attempts—kept as a finding, not a numeric result. Most case studies lack quantifiable scores due to responsible disclosure.
